paper_title: Thinking Slow, Fast Scaling Inference Compute with Distilled Reasoners
caption_used: Coverage as a function of the number of completions (k) for Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT. All four models exhibit monotonically increasing coverage with additional completions on a logarithmic x-axis from 2^0 to 2^8. The 3B models begin at approximately 0.42 coverage and reach roughly 0.92 at k=256, while the 1B variants start near 0.22 and plateau at approximately 0.72 by k=128 with minimal further gains. Notably, fine-tuning provides a consistent advantage of approximately 5 percentage points for the 1B model throughout the scaling curve, whereas the 3B base and fine-tuned variants remain largely indistinguishable.
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the coverage, measured in some unit of accuracy or success, as a function of the number of completions (notated as 'k') for four different models: Llama-3B, Llama-3B with Fine-Tuning (FT), Llama-1B, and Llama-1B with Fine-Tuning. The number of completions is presented on a logarithmic x-axis ranging from 2^0 to 2^8. The coverage values are shown on the y-axis, which appears to start around 0.20 and goes up to approximately 0.90. The Llama-3B model is depicted with a blue line and circles, the Llama-3B + FT with a green line and triangles, the Llama-1B with a light blue line and diamonds, and the Llama-1B + FT with a pink line and asterisks. The plot reveals that the coverage for the Llama-3B and Llama-1B base models increases from around 0.42 to 0.92 and 0.22 to 0.72, respectively, as the number of completions increases. Fine-tuning appears to provide a significant boost to the coverage for the Llama-1B model, increasing its coverage from just below 0.22 to just above 0.72 with little additional gain beyond this point. In contrast, fine-tuning does not seem to provide a clear advantage for the Llama-3B model, as both the base model and the fine-tuned variant show very similar trajectories on the plot.
